confirmed.statement: The paper does not say whether any designer entered both contests. Section 5 says 'We followed the same designer recruitment process as in the main experiment' and that the replication changed incentives and duration 'to assess generalizability across a different distribution of participating designers'. The form flags this. Each study alone exceeds 50.

No other paper shares this sample. Of the 1,002 records in candidates.json, only c131 matches these authors or the Armor Health and Juneberry contests. No other form or literature file does. De Freitas et al. (arXiv 2608.07504, Timoshenko a coauthor) only cites Wu et al. (2026) and reports none of its data.

Caveat, not an error: the notes to Tables 1 and 2 define registered designers as those who viewed the contest information and creative brief. The paper treats registration as the point of randomization and reports no designer randomized but not registered.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 2 holds for each study alone. S1 analyzes 292 designers in four arms (146 in Variation(1) vs Blind). S2 analyzes 208 in three arms (143 in Variation vs Blind). The quality outcome uses every submission, so it covers all analyzed designers in both studies.

summary: The PDF supports every participant count in the c131 form: Study 1 randomized 440 designers at registration and analyzes the 292 who submitted at least one logo (Table 1), and Study 2 lists 485 registered designers by condition and analyzes 208 (Table 2), all counted as designers and kept apart from the 2,199 and 1,027 submissions. Each study alone clears 50 analyzed people, and the two gaps the paper leaves open (how many designers supply the top-50 originality samples, and whether any designer entered both contests) are already flagged in the form and cannot change that.
